summary: This article argues that local governments must act urgently on climate adaptation, using examples of towns and cities from late 2023 through 2024. It covers flood planning, financing, science partnerships, equity, youth engagement, intergovernmental coalitions, technology and green infrastructure. It concludes that adaptation must be built into all local policymaking.
one_line: An article arguing local governments must urgently adopt climate adaptation policy, illustrated by examples in finance, science, equity, youth, collaboration, technology and green infrastructure.
key_facts: Mayor Sarah Jackson of Elmwood Town took office on October 12, 2023 and has spearheaded comprehensive flood management and resilience planning in the flood-prone town.
On November 20, 2023, the Bayside city council discussed its climate action plan; Councilman Rodrigo Vazquez said adaptation must be woven into all local policies.
Bayside's plan includes strict zoning laws to prevent construction in flood-prone areas and green infrastructure such as urban wetlands to absorb stormwater.
On January 15, 2024, the Brookfield Institute released a report stating every dollar spent on strengthening communities saves six dollars in future costs.
GreenBank, a financing hub, launched on February 25, 2024 to support climate adaptation projects, offering local governments attractive loan terms.
On March 10, 2024, Dr. Emily Chen of the National Climate Research Center called for stronger partnerships between researchers and local policymakers.
Lakeview City signed a memorandum of understanding with Westfield University on April 2, 2024 to incorporate climate projections into urban planning.
On May 19, 2024, Maria Gonzales of the Fair Skies Initiative spoke at the Resilient Cities Conference about marginalized neighborhoods lacking infrastructure to withstand climate events.
On June 22, 2024, Northgate City Mayor Juan Hernandez announced an 'Equity in Adaptation' plan to direct resources to low-income communities hit by heatwaves and pollution.
Riverside City formed a Youth Climate Council on August 5, 2024 to advise on policy from a youth perspective.
The United Climate Adaptation Council (UCAC) was formed on September 30, 2024 as a coalition of local governments advocating national support for local adaptation.
The InnoClimate Tech Fair on October 21, 2024 showcased advanced flood prediction models and new materials for roads and buildings that cope with extreme temperatures.
Central Park's 'Living Landscape Initiative' launched on November 12, 2024 to increase resilience to heavy rainfall and heatwaves.
